the combination of CXB and EBRT is an effective treatment for rectal cancer and is associated with a very low morbidity rate.

organ preservation using CXB and EBRT is an effective treatment for T2-T3 tumors and that it is possible to achieve a 5-year local control rate of 85%, a 5-year overall survival of 70% and a 5-year disease-free survival of 65%.

the following question: can organ preservation be achieved in T2-3 rectal adenocrinoma using CXB and EBRT?
the following questions: (1) Is CXB combined with EBRT an effective treatment of rectal adenocancer?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CXB with EB is effective and safe in organ preservation in T3 tumors.
the combined use of CXB and EBRT is an efficient and safe treatment for patients with T2-T3 N0 rectal adenocarinoma, allowing in most cases organ preservation and a good quality of life.
CXB is not a treatment of choice for rectal cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CXB is a safe, efficient and cost effective treatment for T1-2N0 rectal adenocar-cinoma.

the Lyon Sud –Nice experience using combined CXB and EBRT in 120 patients with a median follow-up of 5.6 years (1.2 to 18.2 years) is safe and effective with an overall survival (OS) of 83.5% and local relapse free survival (LRFS) of 89%.
the use of CXBT2-T3 Nx MO is a safe and effective alternative to radical surgery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the absence of randomized studies, organ preservation using CRT with or without CXB can be proposed in T2-T3 tumors as a safe alternative to TME surgery with or without preoperative treatment.
the combination of EBRT and CXB is feasible, well tolerated and can achieve a high rate of cCR with low toxicity and a very low risk of local failure.
in a homogeneous population of patients with rectal adenocancer, the use of combined CXB and EBRT can be a safe and efficient alternative to standard radical surgery.
